source_text:
Ἄσωμεν τὸ ᾆσμα τὸ καινόν, ἰδοὺ γὰρ Ἀδὰμ ἀνεκαινίσθη καὶ Εὔα εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀνεκομίσθη, ὁ γὰρ διάβολος εἰς τὸ
πῦρ ἐσκελίσθη. Χρησώμεθα παρὰ Μαρίας τῆς ἀδελφῆς Μωϋσέως τὸ ᾆσμα ἐκεῖνο, πρέπει γὰρ ἡμῖν νῦν ᾗπερ τότε ἐκείνοις. Συμπαρέστω ἡμῖν καὶ ὁ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκείνων χορὸς καὶ λεγέτω ὃ τότε ἐπὶ τῆς Ἐρυθρᾶς θαλάσσης ἐκελάδιζεν, τό· Ἄσωμεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται. Τί γὰρ πεποίηκεν; Ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην ἔρριψεν εἰς θάλασσαν. Ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην· ἵππον μὲν τὴν θηλυμανῆ ἁμαρτίαν, ἀναβάτην δὲ τὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ καθήμενον δαίμονα ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι τοῦ λουτροῦ κατεπόντισεν. Ἄσωμεν οὖν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται· τὸν γὰρ Φαραὼ καὶ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ ἔρριψεν εἰς θάλασσαν, τουτέστιν τὸν διάβολον καὶ τὸ σκοτεινὸν καὶ ἐναγὲς τῶν δαιμόνων αὐτοῦ στρατόπεδον ἐν τῷ λουτρῷ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἐθαλάσσωσεν. Οὐκέτι φοβοῦμαι ἀκούειν· Γῆ εἶ καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ· ἐν γὰρ τῷ βαπτίσματι τὴν γῆν ἀπεθέμην καὶ οὐρανὸν ἐνεδυσάμην καὶ ἀκούω· οὐρανὸς εἶ καὶ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀπελεύσῃ· ὅσοι γὰρ εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε, καί· οἷος ὁ χοϊκός, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ χοϊκοί, καὶ οἷος ὁ ἐπουράνιος, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ἐπουράνιοι. ∆εῖ ἡμᾶς νεφέλαις ἐπιβῆναι καὶ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀναδραμεῖν· οὐκ ἀμάρτυρος ὁ λόγος, ἄκουε τοῦ Παύλου λέγοντος· Ἁρπαγησόμεθα ἐν νεφέλαις εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ κυρίου εἰς ἀέρα καὶ οὕτως πάντοτε σὺν κυρίῳ ἐσόμεθα. ∆ιὸ καθὼς ἠκούσαμεν ἀρτίως τοῦ ψαλμῳδοῦ ἡμῖν παραινοῦντος καὶ λέγον τος· Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα ἣν ἐποίησεν ὁ κύριος, ἀγαλλιασώμεθα καὶ εὐ φρανθῶμεν ἐν αὐτῇ. Ἀγαλλιασώμεθα οὖν οὐ μέθῃ καὶ κραιπάλῃ σκοτούμενοι, αὕτη γὰρ οὐκ ἂν εἴη εὐφροσύνη ἀλλὰ ἀφροσύνη καὶ σκοτομήνη καρδίας. Ἀγαλλιασώμεθα σκιρτῶντες τῷ πνεύματι, ἀγαλλιασώμεθα ἀγάπῃ ἑστιώμενοι, ἐλπίδι χαίροντες. Εἰ δὲ δεῖ καὶ ἑτέραν ἐννοεῖν εὐφροσύνην καρδίας, τὸν οὐράνιον ἄρτον καθαραῖς παλάμαις ὑποδεξάμενοι τῇ ψυχῇ παραπέμψωμεν ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἐφόδιον ὄντα· καθαραῖς παλάμαις ὑποδεξάμενοι λέγω δέ, οὐχ ὕδατι κοινῷ πεπλυμέναις, ἀλλ' εὐποιΐαις λαμπρυνομέναις. Καὶ τὸ θεῖον καὶ οὐράνιον κρᾶμα ῥοδοείδεσι χείλεσιν ἀρυσώμεθα, οὐ φοίνικί τινι ἐρυθαίνοντες, ἀλλὰ τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πορφυρίζοντες. Ὦ μεγάλης ὡς ἀληθῶς καὶ ἀγαθῆς ἡμέρας, ἐν ᾗ ὁ ἀμνὸς σφαγιάζεται καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἀγοράζεται καὶ ὁ ποιμὴν ἡμῶν ζῇ· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι, φησίν, ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός. Ὦ μυστηρίου καινοῦ καὶ θαύματος παραδόξου! Σταυρὸς ἔστη καὶ Χριστὸς ἐφηπλώθη καὶ θάνατος ἄδικος ἦν τὸ φαινόμενον καὶ θάλαμος ἅγιος ἦν τὸ γινόμενον, σταυρὸς ἦν τὸ φαινόμενον καὶ παστὸς ἦν τὸ τελούμε νον· χθὲς ἀνέστη παστὸς καὶ σήμερον ἐτέχθη λαός. Ὦ θάνατος Χριστοῦ, θανάτου θάνατος καὶ γλυκεῖαν ζωὴν ἐν τῷ πικροτάτῳ θανάτῳ πηγάζων! Ὦ μυστηρίου Ἀβραμιαίου ἐν Χριστῷ τελουμένου!
thought_title: The new song of baptism: horse and rider drowned, the baptized clothed with heaven
orientation: Amphilochius is preaching to the newly baptized, urging them to take up the song of Miriam at the Red Sea as the type of their own baptismal victory.
pass_a_gloss: Let us sing the new song, for behold, Adam has been made new and Eve has been carried up to the heavens, for the devil has been tripped into the fire. Let us borrow from Mary the sister of Moses that song, for it befits us now just as it befitted them then. Let the chorus of those holy ones be present with us also and let it say what it then sang aloud at the Red Sea, namely: Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified. For what has he done? Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea. Horse and rider: the horse, namely the sin that is mad after the female, and the rider, namely the demon sitting upon sin, he sank in the baptism of the washing. Let us sing therefore to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified; for Pharaoh and his power he has thrown into the sea, that is, the devil and the dark and accursed camp of his demons he has made into sea in the washing of baptism. No longer do I fear to hear: Earth you are and to earth you will go; for in baptism I put off the earth and put on heaven and I hear: heaven you are and to the heavens you will go; for as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ, and: as is the man of dust, such also are those of dust, and as is the heavenly man, such also are those of heaven. We must mount upon clouds and run up to the heavens; the word is not without witness, hear Paul saying: We shall be snatched up in clouds to meet the Lord in the air and so we shall always be with the Lord. Therefore just as we heard just now the psalmist urging us and saying: This is the day which the Lord has made, let us rejoice and be glad in it. Let us rejoice therefore, not being darkened with drunkenness and debauchery, for this would not be gladness but foolishness and moon-darkness of heart. Let us rejoice leaping in the Spirit, let us rejoice feasting on love, rejoicing in hope. And if we must also consider another gladness of heart, having received the heavenly bread with pure palms let us send it on to the soul as provision for eternal life; having received it with pure palms, I mean, not palms washed with common water, but palms made bright with good deeds. And let us draw the divine and heavenly mixture with rose-like lips, not reddening them with any crimson dye, but making them purple with the blood of Jesus Christ. O how great truly and good is the day, on which the lamb is slain and the world is purchased and our shepherd lives; For I am, he says, the good shepherd. O new mystery and paradoxical wonder! A cross stood and Christ was stretched out and death unjust was what appeared and a holy bridal chamber was what came to be, a cross was what appeared and a bridal chamber was what was being accomplished; yesterday a bridal chamber arose and today a people was born. O death of Christ, death of death and sweet life welling up in the most bitter death! O mystery of Abraham being accomplished in Christ!

choices.english: the sin that is mad after the female
choices.why: Keeps the compound adjective's force literally: sin is personified as lusting after the female, matching the horse image from Exodus 15.
The verb is a rare denominative from θάλασσα; rendering it as 'made into sea' preserves the wordplay with the Red Sea and the baptismal washing.
Σκοτομήνη is the dark of the moon; the literal rendering keeps the contrast with the day's light and the play on εὐφροσύνη/ἀφροσύνη.
Παστός is the bridal chamber or marriage bower; the literal rendering preserves the nuptial imagery of the cross as the place where Christ and the people are joined.
The verb means to be spread out or extended upon something; 'stretched out' keeps the physical image of Christ on the cross.
The verb means to draw liquid, as from a well; 'draw' keeps the image of drawing the divine mixture with the lips.

pass_b_english: Let us sing the new song, for behold, Adam has been made new and Eve has been carried up to the heavens, and the devil has been thrown into the fire. Let us borrow that song from Miriam, the sister of Moses, for it suits us now just as it suited them then. Let the chorus of those saints stand with us and sing what they sang aloud then at the Red Sea: “Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified” (Exodus 15:1). What has he done? “Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:10). Horse and rider: the horse is lust-mad sin, and the rider is the demon seated upon sin, and in the baptismal washing he sank them both. Let us sing then to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified, for “Pharaoh and his power he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:4)—that is, the devil and his dark and defiled army of demons he drowned in the washing of baptism. I no longer fear to hear, “Earth you are, and to earth you shall return” (Genesis 3:19), for in baptism I put off the earth and put on heaven, and I hear: Heaven you are, and to the heavens you shall return. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ, and: As is the man of dust, so are those who are of dust; and as is the man of heaven, so are those who are of heaven (1 Corinthians 15:48). We must mount upon the clouds and run up to the heavens. The word is not without witness; hear Paul saying: “We shall be caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord” (1 Thessalonians 4:17). Therefore, as we have just heard the psalmist urging us and saying, “This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it” (Psalm 118:24 (117:24 LXX)), let us rejoice then, not darkened by drunkenness and dissipation—for that would not be gladness but folly and darkening of heart. Let us rejoice, leaping in the Spirit; let us rejoice, feasting on love, rejoicing in hope. And if we must also consider another gladness of heart, let us receive the heavenly bread with pure hands and send it on to the soul as provision for eternal life. With pure hands, I say—not washed with ordinary water, but made bright by good deeds. And let us draw the divine and heavenly mixture with rose-colored lips, reddening them not with any crimson dye but making them purple with the blood of Jesus Christ. O truly great and good day, on which the lamb is slain and the world is purchased and our shepherd lives! For he says, “I am the good shepherd” (John 10:11). O new mystery and strange wonder! The cross stood and Christ was stretched out, and what appeared was an unjust death, but what was happening was a holy bridal chamber; what appeared was a cross, but what was being accomplished was a bridal chamber. Yesterday the bridal chamber was set up, and today a people was born. O death of Christ, death of death, pouring forth sweet life in the bitterest death! O mystery of Abraham being accomplished in Christ!

problems.quote: the horse is the sin that is mad after the female
problems.why: Greek says ‘the female sin’, not ‘sin mad after the female’.
problems.fix: Render as “the horse is the female sin”.

problems.why: ἐθαλάσσωσεν means 'drowned/sank in the sea', not 'made into sea'
problems.fix: he drowned in the washing of baptism
problems.ruling: ἐθαλάσσωσεν means ‘threw into the sea/drowned’, not ‘made into sea’

problems.why: ἀνέστη means 'rose/stand up', but here refers to Christ's resurrection from the bridal chamber/tomb
problems.ruling: ἀνέστη παστὸς means ‘the bridegroom rose’, not ‘the bridal chamber arose’

problems.source_quote: Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα ἣν ἐποίησεν ὁ κύριος
problems.why: Psalm 117:24 LXX = Psalm 118:24 Hebrew; should note LXX numbering differs

problems.quote: “Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:1)
problems.source_quote: Ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην ἔρριψεν εἰς θάλασσαν.
problems.why: The cited verse is Exodus 15:10, not 15:1.
problems.ruling: Greek quotes Ex 15:1 (Ἄσωμεν τῷ κυρίῳ) but horse/rider is Ex 15:1b or 15:21, not 15:10.

edits.old: the horse is the sin that is mad after the female
edits.new: the horse is the female sin

edits.old: he has made into sea in the washing of baptism
edits.new: he drowned in the washing of baptism

edits.old: “Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:1)
edits.new: “Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:10)

fixed: Corrected 'the horse is the sin that is mad after the female' to 'the horse is the female sin' based on θηλυμανῆ ἁμαρτίαν.
Corrected 'he has made into sea' to 'he drowned' based on ἐθαλάσσωσεν.
Corrected 'the bridal chamber arose' to 'the bridal chamber rose' based on ἀνέστη παστὸς.
Corrected Psalm citation to Psalm 118:24 (117:24 LXX).

problems.source_quote: Ἄσωμεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται (Exodus 15:2 in the LXX)
problems.why: The verse quoted is Exodus 15:2 in the Septuagint; the citation should be 15:2, not 15:1.
problems.fix: Change the citation to “(Exodus 15:2)” (or note the LXX numbering if different).

problems.ruling: σκοτομήνη = darkness, not ‘moon‑darkness’; translation misrenders meaning.

problems.quote: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ (Galatians 3:27)
problems.source_quote: ὅσοι γὰρ εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε, καί… (1 Cor 15:48)
problems.why: The source cites 1 Cor 15:48 only; the Galatians 3:27 reference is not in the Greek text.
problems.fix: Remove the parenthetical “(Galatians 3:27)” and keep the quotation as in the source.
problems.ruling: Source has no Galatians citation; only 1 Cor 15:48 follows. Added reference misleads.

fixed: The verse quoted is Exodus 15:2 in the Septuagint, so the citation is corrected to (Exodus 15:2).
σκοτομήνη means 'darkening/eclipse', not 'moon-darkness', so the English is corrected to 'darkening of heart'.
The source does not include a Galatians 3:27 citation; the parenthetical is removed.

problems.why: θηλυμανῆ means 'mad after women/lustful', not 'female'; the horse is lustful sin, not feminine sin.
problems.ruling: Translates θηλυμανῆ as 'female' sin, losing sense of lustful sin.

problems.source_quote: Ἄσωμεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται
problems.why: The quote matches Exodus 15:1 (LXX), not 15:2; 15:2 begins 'βοηθὸς καὶ σκεπαστής'.
problems.ruling: Cites Exodus 15:2 but phrase belongs to Exodus 15:1 in LXX (mis‑numbered).

problems.why: ἀνέστη means 'rose' in sense of resurrection, but παστὸς here refers to Christ (the bridegroom) who rose; 'bridal chamber rose' obscures that Christ the bridegroom rose.
problems.ruling: Renders χθὲς ἀνέστη παστὸς as 'bridal chamber rose', obscuring that the bridegroom rose.

problems.quote: devil has been tripped into the fire
problems.source_quote: ὁ γὰρ διάβολος εἰς τὸ πῦρ ἐσκελίσθη
problems.why: Greek says devil was cast/thrown into fire; "tripped" misstates the action.
problems.fix: devil has been thrown into the fire
problems.ruling: ἐσκελίσθη is passive of σκελίζω, 'to hamstring, disable, throw down'; 'tripped' understates the violent casting-into-fire action.

fixed: θηλυμανῆ means 'mad after women/lustful', not 'female'; changed to 'lust-mad sin'.
The quote matches Exodus 15:1 (LXX), not 15:2; changed citation.
παστὸς here refers to Christ the bridegroom who rose; changed to 'bridegroom rose'.
ἐσκελίσθη means 'was thrown/cast', not 'tripped'; changed to 'thrown'.

fixed.quote: Yesterday the bridegroom rose, and today a people was born.
fixed.fix: Yesterday the bridal chamber was set up, and today a people was born.
fixed.note: παστός means bridal chamber, not bridegroom, and ἀνέστη here means 'was set up'; the proposed 'the past rose' is nonsense.

dismissed.why: Greek says “the feminine sin,” not “lust‑mad sin”; adds unwarranted notion of lust.
dismissed.note: θηλυμανής means 'mad for women', so 'lust-mad' is fair; 'feminine sin' misreads the word.
